laws.rule: Non-residents 21 and over may possess up to 15 g of cannabis flower, 2.5 g of concentrate and 250 mg THC in infused products (residents have higher limits); public consumption is prohibited. Cannabis remains illegal under US federal law, including on federal land such as national parks.
Non-residents do not need a FOID card but must be eligible to possess firearms at home; a firearm being transported must be broken down, not immediately accessible, or unloaded and cased.

Chicago's Municipal Code (section 8-4-030) makes it unlawful to drink alcohol on a public way, or in or about a vehicle on a public way, with exceptions such as licensed sidewalk cafes and certain Navy Pier areas. Separately, section 10-36-100 bars bringing in or drinking intoxicating liquor in a public park, playground or bathing beach.
laws.penalty_signal: fine of US$100 to US$500, or up to six months in jail, or both, for public-way drinking (about A$142 to A$710 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: The Chicago Park District's beach rules say no alcohol and no smoking on the beaches, and swim only when lifeguards are on duty (11 am to 7 pm, from the Friday before Memorial Day through Labor Day). The page lists no dogs on the beach and grilling in designated areas only.

The Illinois State Fire Marshal says possessing, selling, using and displaying fireworks is prohibited in Illinois except in villages, counties and municipalities that have passed an ordinance allowing consumer displays, and only there. Consumer fireworks must be on the Marshal's approved list, and a consumer display needs an adult operator who has trained, a local fire-jurisdiction site approval and a local permit applied for at least 15 days ahead. The Marshal does not issue these permits. Handheld items such as firecrackers, Roman candles and bottle rockets are not approved.

On Illinois Department of Natural Resources land, it is unlawful to possess or consume alcohol (including beer and wine) where signs say alcohol is prohibited. Bans differ by site and season: some cover the whole park, others only campgrounds, beaches or hunting areas. A violation is a Class B misdemeanor, payable by mail for $75 (about A$107 at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Class B misdemeanor; US$75 by mail

items.text: Adults 21 and over who are not Illinois residents may possess up to 30 g of cannabis flower, 5 g of concentrate and 500 mg of THC in infused products; residents 60 g, 10 g and 1,000 mg. The limits are cumulative (410 ILCS 705/10-10, as amended by P.A. 104-463 from 12 June 2026).
